findings.mechanism: The focus word for sending-down names divine delivery, while the focus Book carries both the act of writing and its written product. The next ayah's accusation and answer meet those carriers: what first appears as a delivered text is now seen as a text being challenged and affirmed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the Book is named as both delivered and written: the pericope immediately places that materialized message in a dispute about who sent it and what it is.
findings.containment: The 32:3 text supplies the dispute and answer at the surface level; its target morphology is not supplied, so no separate lexical branch is claimed for speech or truth. The source clause still says that the Book is from the Lord.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and channel supports are supplied as trusted, and the connection directly identifies 32:3 as answering the fabrication accusation. Context morphology is absent, and the two unresolved channel branch citations are not activated.

Certainty is thus stated inside a live exchange and toward a newly addressed audience.

The warning is retained as the verse's stated purpose, while the channel's separate sewing, falsehood, woven-speech, and alarm branches remain unactivated because their branch records and target morphology are absent.

findings.title: Two attributed pictures of textual making
findings.claim: The Book remains the written text named in 32:2, while the next ayah's accusation allows an attributed assembly image to arise: one side pictures a text joined into a whole, and the rival accusation is carried as cutting, sewing, and false construction; the answer as truth supplies the counter-image of tightly fitted discourse. In that exchange, no doubt also names textual integrity under pressure.
findings.mechanism: Where a flat reading leaves no doubt as only an assertion that the Book is true, the registered joining branch meets the exact following accusation and truth claim, and the focus doubt branch meets that accusation as its public pressure. The HFT's attributed readings of the context words then supply cutting and sewing, fabrication, and tightly wrought speech, changing the reading into a contrast between rival ways of making discourse.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a local image of coherent text against a charge of constructed falsehood, with the Book's integrity stated at the point where its making is challenged.
findings.containment: The joining branch is not the lexical meaning of kitāb; its own boundary excludes the written Book, so it survives only as a contextual root-image. The three context-branch roles are attributed from a legacy-unbound HFT trace because target morphology and independent lexicon records are absent. The HFT also allows the alternative that writing, fabrication, and truth remain separate idioms.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic and the connection establish the focus-to-context contact, but the reader identity is unbound and the context branch mappings are attributed. The assembly synthesis remains a bounded writer inference rather than an independently verified lexical reading.

findings.title: The descent within an administrative circuit

Its source phrase still names a delivered Book, while the following account of management, affair, ascent, and measure lets that delivery be read within the world's administration.
findings.mechanism: The focus delivery branch carries the Book downward, and the focus Book can also carry the branch of binding determination. In 32:5, attributed context carriers name management of an affair, upward return, and measured timing; those images meet the focus delivery and determination, changing simple high-to-low travel into a possible incoming movement within a governed circuit.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the descent as one leg of a larger order that moves from heaven to earth and returns in measured time, while the Book's relation to that order remains an analogy.
findings.containment: The HFT reader explicitly allows that 32:5 may only identify the sender and not describe the Book's function; the authored connection likewise treats the sky-to-earth movement as an echo of governance rather than proof of the Book's descent. The relation is retained as an attributed analogy, and the Book's ordinary delivery remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The 32:2 and 32:5 Arabic anchors and all four context word coordinates are supplied, but context morphology and branch records are absent. The HFT model is legacy-unbound and itself states the live alternative; the connection note limits how directly 32:5 describes the Book.

friction_notes: The focus word-alignment bridge resolves all 8 analysis entries and reports no unresolved units, so none of the focus readings was suppressed by a missing join.

The supplied 32:3, 32:5, and 32:9 context anchors include exact Arabic but no target morphology. HFT word coordinates, roots, and roles are therefore treated as attributed; the channel citations for unregistered 32:3 branches are not promoted to independent lexical findings.

The administrative-circuit HFT includes a structural cue to 32:4, but its supplied anchor Arabic covers only 32:2 and 32:5. The retained reading relies on the exact 32:5 text and does not depend on the unanchored 32:4 cue.

The HFT assembly reading itself preserves the alternative that joining, fabrication, and truth remain separate idioms; the integrated assembly contrast is exploratory and does not lexicalize kitab as joining.

The 32:9 recipient reading has the HFT's alternative that human creation only establishes the sender's power, and the supplied connection also cautions that 32:9 directly concerns human faculties rather than the Book.

The declared pericope spans 32:1-10, while exact non-focus Arabic is supplied here for 32:3, 32:5, 32:7, 32:9, and the automatic host basmala 32:0. No finding uses unsupplied text from other pericope members.
